answer: A credit-network protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by bounding agent interactions to pre-funded trust channels. Because network flow cannot exceed the credit river established between authentic peers, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locking collateral per synthetic node. Each peering contract is signed by an agent's cryptographic quill. A key limitation is that when transient tasks flash like a comet, rigid channel limits partition honest agents with low bilateral credit.
